attention.whatHappened: Adds ticket transfer (a `holder_id` column, a service, a REST route and a form), but the cancel-and-refund path still checks only the booker.
attention.why: Money and access: the old owner can still refund an order they gave away, and nothing checks the event start, which contradicts criteria 3 and 5 of the spec.

whatItDoes: Adds a nullable `orders.holder_id`, a `transferOrder` service that sets it after an owner and email check, `POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/transfer`, and a Transfer form on the order page. My orders and the order page now follow the holder. The branch also carries three unrelated sandbox fixes, a global Playwright `retries: 2`, and the adversarial reviewer's failing tests and findings doc.
why: A customer can give the tickets of a paid order to a friend.
points: a nullable [holder_id](drizzle/0003_order_holder.sql:1) column; [holderOf](src/db/orders-repo.ts:47) falls back to the booker
[transferOrder](src/services/transfers.ts:16) checks holder, `paid` and the friend's account, then calls [setHolder](src/db/orders-repo.ts:62); it reads no clock and no event
[My orders](src/db/orders-repo.ts:56) and the [order page](app/(public)/orders/[id]/page.tsx:31) follow the holder; `cancelOwnOrder` (outside the diff) still compares `userId`
the branch commits the [adversarial tests](tests/integration/transfers.adversarial.test.ts) and a [findings doc](docs/reviews/ticket-transfer-findings.md:81) that says 7 of them fail

shape.title: Who counts as the owner, per path
shape.code:
holderOf(order) = order.holderId ?? order.userId

GET  /orders/{id} page      -> holderOf(order) === session   (changed)
listOrdersByUser (My orders, MCP my_orders)
                            -> holderId = me OR (holderId IS NULL AND userId = me)   (changed)
transferOrder               -> holderOf(order) === caller     (new)
  setHolder                 -> WHERE id AND status = 'paid'   (no holder condition)
cancelOwnOrder (REST, MCP refund_order, cancelOrderAction)
                            -> order.userId === caller        (unchanged)

claims.quote: A transfer is possible only before the event starts.
claims.note: The service checks status only; it takes no clock and never loads the event. Check a transfer one hour after the start.

claims.quote: A transferred ticket can't be refunded by the old owner.
claims.note: `cancelOwnOrder` in `src/services/orders.ts` still compares `found.userId`, not `holderOf`. Check the booker's cancel after a transfer.

claims.quote: Only the order's owner can transfer its tickets.
claims.note: This lets the current holder transfer, not only the booker. Check which one "owner" means.

claims.quote: After the transfer, the friend sees the ticket in My orders, and the owner no longer does.
claims.note: Check the booker's list when the holder is set, and the friend's list after a transfer back to the booker.

Now it exits 2 with
'jq is missing: install it (see the setup guide)'.
claims.note: `block` exits 2; check it runs before the `jq` read, on a PATH without jq.

items.title: Does every ownership check use holderOf? cancelOwnOrder does not
items.why: `cancelOwnOrder` (`src/services/orders.ts:338`, outside the diff) still checks `found.userId`. It backs `POST /orders/{id}/cancel`, MCP `refund_order` and `cancelOrderAction`. Check whether the booker can refund an order after giving it away (criterion 5).

items.title: No check against the event start
items.why: `transferOrder` takes `{ db }` only, with no `nowMs`, and never reads the event. The page shows the form for any paid order (`page.tsx:131`). Criterion 3 says before the event starts only.

items.title: The holder now sees the refund preview and Cancel form
items.why: The page admits the holder, but cancel accepts only the booker, so Bela's Cancel fails. The spec does not say who may cancel a transferred order, or whose card the refund goes to.

items.title: setHolder does not check the holder it read
items.why: The holder check runs on a read in `transferOrder`; the update filters only on id and status. Check two concurrent transfers, or a stale one landing after the order moved on.

items.code: No TicketBay account uses this email
items.title: This message tells a caller whether an email has an account
items.why: Any write-scoped API key with one paid order can probe emails with no rate limit. Check whether this answer is a decision someone made.

items.title: A friend who received tickets can pass them on
items.why: The check is the current holder, so transfers chain. Criterion 1 says "the order's owner"; check whether that means the booker.

items.title: Every e2e test now retries twice; no commit mentions it
items.why: This is global, so a flaky money-path test passes on its second or third run. The comment below says failures there must be diagnosable without a rerun.

items.code: The only failures are the 7 new adversarial tests.
items.title: The branch commits tests its own record says fail
items.why: Merging this as-is makes the integration and HTTP suites red. Some `[undecided]` tests also fix a decision the spec leaves open (e.g. `transfers.adversarial.test.ts:65` expects the holder's cancel to refund). Check which of them are meant to stay.

fileNotes.drizzle/0003_order_holder.sql:
**Adds a nullable `holder_id` with a foreign key and an index; drops nothing.**

- `ON DELETE no action`, the same as `user_id`

**Three helpers decide who holds an order.**
- `holderOf`: `holderId ?? userId`
- `listOrdersByUser` now lists held orders, not booked ones; MCP `my_orders` also calls it
- `setHolder` updates where `status = 'paid'`, with no holder condition and no row lock

**The transfer rules: holder, paid, valid email, existing account, not yourself.**
